Title: Malaysians in Jakarta advised to remain calm following earthquake
Article:
JAKARTA: Malaysians residing in or visiting Jakarta and its surrounding areas are advised to stay calm and keep up-to-date with official information issued by local authorities, following a magnitude 6.5 earthquake that struck near the capital's Thousand Islands (Kepulauan Seribu) early Saturday morning.
The Embassy of Malaysia in Jakarta in a statement today informed that the earthquake did not have the potential to trigger a tsunami and that as of noon, there have yet to be reports of accidents or damages arising from the incident.
"Overseas-bound Malaysians are advised to plan their journeys accordingly, including by allocating extra funds for personal needs, in addition to getting adequately insured prior to departure," the embassy said.
Indonesia's Meteorology, Climatology, and Geophysics Agency (BMKG) recorded the
earthquake
at 4.23am local time, with tremors felt in the Indonesian capital and in across parts of Java and Sumatra.
For consular assistance, Malaysians may contact the Embassy of Malaysia in Jakarta at its fixed line +62 21 522 4947 or WhatsApp or call +62 813 8081 3036.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Kelantan Umno leader says sorry to Pas for 'three villains' remark
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Kelantan Umno delegate Datuk Zawawi Othman has apologised to Pas for referring to some of its leaders as the 'three villains'.
"Pas, I apologise. I previously called them the 'three villains'. That was then.
"Now, I extend my hand in the spirit of goodwill so that we can uphold our religion in our country and unite our people without denying other communities in this country.
"Let us work together to defend our religion, our people and our country. Let us do this together," he said while debating the Umno president's policy speech at the 2026 Umno general assembly.
Zawawi, who is also Kelantan Umno information chief and known for his outspoken criticism of Pas, had previously said Umno could not work with the party as long as the 'three villains' remained in its leadership.
The three leaders he referred to were Pas president Tan Sri Abdul Hadi Awang, Pas election director Datuk Seri Muhammad Sanusi Md Nor and Pas vice-president Datuk Mohd Amar Nik Abdullah.
Zawawi had said they were labelled as such because he regarded them as being 'sharp-tongued'.
Explaining his decision to apologise, Zawawi said it was prompted by recent political developments involving Umno and Pas.
In the same speech, he said Umno had no intention of being hostile towards Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
However, he said the party was unhappy with what he alleged was Anwar's tendency to follow advice from those around him.
"We do not hate you, but we see that you have listened too much to those advising you around you and have been too compliant with DAP's demands," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malaysia, Ethiopia to hold first bilateral talks in KL next year
Article:
NEW DELHI: Malaysia and Ethiopia will convene their first bilateral consultation in Kuala Lumpur next year as both countries seek to build on growing diplomatic momentum following reciprocal visits by their leaders.
The agreement was reached during Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim's meeting with Ethiopian Prime Minister Dr Abiy Ahmed Ali on the sidelines of the 18th BRICS Leaders' Summit.
The meeting also highlighted the strengthening of bilateral relations following Abiy's visit to Malaysia in 2024 and Anwar's visit to Ethiopia in 2025.
Malaysia's reopening of its embassy in Addis Ababa in September 2025, after a 43-year hiatus, was also cited as a significant step in deepening ties between the two countries.
Anwar expressed appreciation for Ethiopia's support for Malaysia's engagement with BRICS, as Malaysia seeks to use the grouping to expand economic and diplomatic ties with emerging markets.
Anwar also invited Ethiopia to establish an embassy in Kuala Lumpur, which would further strengthen diplomatic representation and facilitate closer government-to-government and business engagement.
The first bilateral consultation in Kuala Lumpur next year is expected to provide a platform for both sides to review existing cooperation and identify new areas for collaboration.
The engagement comes as Malaysia seeks to broaden its economic and diplomatic partnerships across Africa, with Ethiopia viewed as an important gateway to the continent's growing markets.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Anwar calls for 'maximum restraint' as Middle East conflict drags on
Article:
NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has called on all parties to exercise "maximum restraint" amid the continued conflict in the Middle East.
During a bilateral meeting with Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian on the sidelines of the 18th BRICS Leaders' Summit, Anwar expressed Malaysia's "deep concern" over the conflict and escalating tensions across the region.
He warned of broader risks to regional peace, stability and the global economy should the conflict continue.
Anwar also stressed the importance of maintaining the freedom, safety and security of maritime navigation through the Strait of Hormuz, a critical international shipping route and major artery for global energy supplies.
He also called for a return to dialogue and diplomacy to resolve differences and reduce tensions.
The 20-minute meeting at The Oberoi Hotel marked Anwar's first bilateral engagement at the start of his BRICS programme.
Anwar also welcomed the longstanding diplomatic relations between Malaysia and Iran and reaffirmed Malaysia's commitment to strengthening bilateral cooperation across various areas of mutual interest.
Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani, Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri R. Ramanan and other members of the Malaysian delegation also attended.
The two leaders are also expected to explore opportunities to expand bilateral trade and investment, particularly in areas including energy, agriculture, palm oil, food security, the halal economy, technology and higher education.
The meeting comes as Malaysia seeks to leverage its BRICS membership to broaden economic engagement with emerging markets, with Iran's membership providing another avenue for trade, investment and economic cooperation.
The two countries have previously identified areas for closer cooperation, including trade, investment, education, healthcare and research.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malaysia, Ethiopia explore wider economic cooperation across key sectors
Article:
NEW DELHI: Malaysia and Ethiopia are exploring wider economic cooperation in halal products, agriculture, food security, pharmaceuticals, digital services, renewable energy and tourism as both countries seek to turn closer diplomatic ties into commercial opportunities.
The areas were discussed during Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim's bilateral meeting with Ethiopian Prime Minister Dr Abiy Ahmed Ali on the sidelines of the 18th BRICS Leaders' Summit here.
The two leaders discussed opportunities to expand cooperation across sectors, with potential to boost trade, investment and private-sector participation.
Malaysia's expertise in the halal economy could support cooperation with Ethiopia in halal products, certification, food processing and related industries.
Agriculture and food security were also identified as potential areas for closer collaboration, particularly as countries seek to strengthen food supply resilience and agricultural productivity.
The two countries could also explore partnerships in pharmaceuticals and digital services through business-to-business cooperation, technology partnerships and knowledge exchange.
Renewable energy and tourism were also identified as areas with potential for deeper engagement, creating opportunities for investment and technical cooperation.
The discussions form part of Malaysia's broader efforts to strengthen economic ties with African economies and identify new markets for Malaysian companies.
The first Malaysia-Ethiopia Bilateral Consultation, scheduled to be held in Kuala Lumpur next year, is expected to provide a platform to further develop these areas of cooperation and identify specific projects and commercial opportunities.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Zambry meets students, stakeholders over new law replacing Auku
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Higher Education Minister Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abdul Kadir has met student representatives as part of efforts to draft a new law to replace the Universities and University Colleges Act 1971 (Auku).
Zambry said he had also begun discussions with various groups, including academics, university administrators and other stakeholders, to ensure their views were taken into account in formulating the new legislation.
"We are working on it now. I have started discussions with all groups because I do not want any group to be left out when we create a new Act to replace Auku.
"I have held several meetings with representatives from the academic community, administrators, including those outside Category A (universities), and in the next few days I will also meet other groups," he said on the sidelines of the 2026 Umno general assembly today.
Zambry said student groups were also being consulted, including student representative councils.
"I have met with student representative councils and I have also asked the national student representative council, which represents universities nationwide, to hold their own discussions, including with groups that may agree or disagree.
"We will bring all these views together because I want a comprehensive Act that takes into account all perspectives. We want to create a new Act not just for today, but for the future of the country," he said.
He said the government needed to anticipate future developments when drafting the legislation, given that Auku was enacted 54 years ago.
"When we want to plan, we have to plan for the future as well. So, we need to anticipate what will happen in terms of the legal framework that exists today and create a comprehensive Act.
"I have said repeatedly that Auku was created 54 years ago. Of course, there will be changes," he said.
He said the new legislation would cover broader aspects of higher education, including the establishment of universities and governance, in addition to matters involving students.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim had announced on Aug 15 that Auku would be repealed to provide students with greater freedom and wider democratic space.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malaysia's strategic location draws local, global drug syndicates
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's proximity to the "Golden Triangle" spanning Thailand, Myanmar and Laos has led drug cartels to use the country as a transit hub for the distribution of illicit drugs.
Bukit Aman Narcotics Crime Investigation Department (NCID) director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said that apart from Malaysia's strategic location, local and international syndicates were also exploiting social visit passes to enter the country and carry out illegal activities.
He said these factors made Malaysia attractive to criminals as a hub or transit country for drug trafficking and smuggling activities by land, air and sea.
"Drug syndicates have long established themselves in Malaysia because of the country's geographical location near the Golden Triangle, which is a major route for drug distribution in Asia and to other continents.
"Malaysia's well-developed ecosystem, in terms of its road network, air and sea transport connectivity as well as other services, is being fully exploited by both local and international syndicates," he said when contacted today.
Hussein was commenting following a string of major police busts that highlighted a trend of foreign and domestic cartels setting up clandestine processing laboratories and distribution networks within the country.
Earlier this week, it was reported that the
drug laboratory
located at Puncak Alam was believed to have been churning out billions of ringgit worth of drugs.
The operation came crashing down on Aug 15 when the Narcotics Crime Investigation Department (NCID) raided the premises as part of Op Eumenes, seizing more than 13 tonnes of liquid and powdered MDMA and other drugs estimated to be worth a staggering RM2.4 billion.
The raid was part of six simultaneous and follow-up raids conducted around Selangor and Kuala Lumpur following intelligence and surveillance on the syndicate.
Police seized about 7.09 tonnes of liquid MDMA and 6.06 tonnes of MDMA powder.
Also seized were 1.04kg of cannabis, 880g of Erimin 5 pills, 180g of ketamine, 150g of yaba pills and 50g of methamphetamine.
It was also reported that the man shot dead by police during a recent anti-drug operation in Seremban is believed to have been the
mastermind
behind the drug laboratory.
Investigations showed that the man headed the syndicate operating the clandestine laboratory.
He was responsible for bringing in equipment from overseas and recruiting other syndicate members.
In July, a
Malaysian pilot was arrested
for allegedly attempting to smuggle a large quantity of drugs, including more than 70,000 ecstasy pills weighing 25kg, into Indonesia.
Indonesian authorities seized over 70,000 ecstasy pills weighing 25kg, 2.74g of methamphetamine, and a glass pipe containing methamphetamine residue. The suspect tested positive for methamphetamine, MDMA, and cocaine, and remains in Indonesian custody.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malaysia, Iran seek broader trade and investment ties
Article:
NEW DELHI: Malaysia and Iran are seeking to broaden trade and investment ties across energy, agriculture, food security, palm oil, the halal economy, technology and higher education.
At their bilateral meeting, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim and Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian discussed expanding existing commercial ties.
They also spoke about encouraging greater participation by companies and private-sector investors.
Malaysia-Iran bilateral trade stood at RM2.45 billion in 2025, with Malaysian exports accounting for RM2.17 billion. Major exports included palm oil, while imports from Iran included oil and gas products.
The two leaders agreed on the need to identify high-potential sectors and projects that could be pursued through government agencies, ministries and the private sector, with the aim of translating bilateral discussions into concrete investment and commercial opportunities.
Energy was among the key areas identified for deeper cooperation, with both sides exploring opportunities related to energy security, efficiency and the transition towards more sustainable energy systems.
Iran's significant energy resources, combined with Malaysia's capabilities across the broader energy value chain, provide scope for mutually beneficial cooperation, subject to applicable international laws, regulations and requirements.
Anwar and Pezeshkian also discussed strengthening cooperation in agriculture and food security amid growing concerns over the resilience of global food supply chains.
Malaysia's position as a major palm oil producer offers another avenue for expanding bilateral trade, including greater market access for Malaysian palm oil and palm-based products in Iran and potentially the wider region.
The two leaders also explored opportunities to deepen cooperation in the halal economy, leveraging Malaysia's internationally recognised halal ecosystem and expertise in areas including standards, certification, food, pharmaceuticals, cosmetics and related industries.
Technology, digitalisation and innovation were also identified as potential areas for closer collaboration, including partnerships involving companies, research institutions, universities and technology ecosystems in both countries.
Higher education and research cooperation also formed part of the discussions, with opportunities for greater academic exchanges, institutional partnerships and joint research.
The discussions underscore Malaysia's push to strengthen economic ties with Iran while broadening cooperation beyond traditional trade into sectors with longer-term commercial potential.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Ramanan: Anwar's Tamil Nadu engagement dropped due to scheduling
Article:
NEW DELHI: Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri R. Ramanan has urged parties to stop politicising and sensationalising the decision not to proceed with a planned engagement in Tamil Nadu during Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim's India visit.
Ramanan said the change to Anwar's itinerary was due to scheduling constraints, with the Prime Minister's programme already packed with high-level bilateral meetings, business engagements and his participation in the 18th BRICS Leaders' Summit.
He was responding to speculation in Malaysian and Indian media over a potential meeting between Anwar and Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay during the prime minister's visit to India.
Vijay, however, left Chennai on Sept 10 for an official delegation to Europe, beginning in London, and is scheduled to return to India only on Sept 17.
As a result, Anwar has adjusted his itinerary and will travel directly from New Delhi to Kerala on Sept 13 before proceeding to the Maldives on Sept 15.
Ramanan dismissed claims that the change was linked to any political consideration, describing such reports as irresponsible and urging an end to what he called the spread of false information.
"This is from certain irresponsible parties, and that's why I want to put it on record and clear this matter, so that this fake news mongering is put to rest," he told Malaysian media on the sidelines of the 18th BRICS Leaders' Summit today.
Ramanan said Anwar's programme had been exceptionally tight, with the prime minister holding meetings with Russian President Vladimir Putin, Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian, Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi and the prime minister of Ethiopia, alongside engagements with major business leaders and companies.
He said the Malaysian delegation would continue with several business meetings today before attending the main BRICS Leaders' Summit tomorrow, followed by Anwar's visit to Kerala and subsequently the Maldives.
"The main problem that we faced was a scheduling issue," Ramanan said, stressing that the change was not due to any particular party or political consideration.
He said a possible engagement in Tamil Nadu had initially been considered as part of Anwar's itinerary between New Delhi and Kerala, but the schedules of the respective offices could not ultimately be aligned.
"Both the Chief Minister's Office and the Prime Minister's Office were trying to get the dates properly organised. But we could not get the dates properly organised because there were so many other events taking place," he said.
Ramanan said Anwar's packed proramme reflected the importance of his participation in the BRICS summit and the opportunity to engage directly with world leaders and major business groups.
He said the prime minister's meetings had focused on strengthening bilateral ties and generating economic opportunities for Malaysia, including in areas such as investment, healthcare and agriculture.
Ramanan said there was no confirmed date for a future engagement with the Tamil Nadu chief minister, as Anwar's schedule remained subject to numerous high-level meetings and requests for engagements with other world leaders.
He also said several leaders were expected to visit Malaysia, including the prime ministers of Iran and Ethiopia, providing further opportunities to follow up on issues discussed during the current India visit.
Ramanan said Anwar's itinerary remained tightly scheduled, with the prime minister due to travel to Kerala before proceeding to the Maldives and returning to Malaysia ahead of Malaysia Day.
He urged parties not to attach political motives to a scheduling matter, saying such speculation could undermine the broader objectives of Anwar's international engagements.
"They should put the country first; politics comes second," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Police nab 2 men, seizes drugs after 50km chase in Kota Tinggi
Article:
JOHOR BARU: Police arrested two men after a 50km high-speed chase involving members of the mobile patrol vehicle unit of the Crime Prevention and Community Safety Department, Kota Tinggi district police headquarters early today.
Kota Tinggi police chief superintendent Yusof Othman said the incident occurred at about 12.35am when policemen ordered a Proton Wira to stop at Jalan Tun Sri Lanang, Bandar Kota Tinggi.
"However, the suspects sped off, driving recklessly.
"A high-speed chase ensued for about 50km, from Jalan Tun Sri Lanang, Bandar Kota Tinggi towards Ulu Tiram before ending at Km31.5 of Jalan Johor Baru-Mersing, near the Taman Sri Saujana traffic lights in Kota Tinggi," he said in a statement today.
He said swift action by the policemen resulted in the vehicle being stopped and the arrest of two men, aged 33 and 44.
Yusof said further checks on the two suspects and the vehicle they were travelling in led to the discovery of drugs believed to be methamphetamine.
He said checks on their records also found that both suspects have previous narcotics offences and are wanted by police under Section 15(1)(a) of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952.
He said the suspects also tested positive for methamphetamine.
"The two suspects have been remanded for four days until Sept 15 to assist in investigations.
"The case is being investigated under Sections 15(1)(a) and 12(2) of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952, as well as Section 186 of the Penal Code," he said.
Earlier, a video circulated on the Threads account @3niee showing a team of police personnel arresting several individuals in a car that was stuck in a traffic congestion.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Blue Malaysia Agenda to be included in BN GE16 manifesto, says Zambry
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Umno's Blue Malaysia Agenda will be incorporated into Barisan Nasional's manifesto for the 16th General Election (GE16), said Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abdul Kadir.
The BN secretary-general said the agenda, outlined by Umno president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi in his policy speech at the 2026 Umno General Assembly, would be translated into the coalition's election manifesto.
"Yes, definitely. It will certainly be translated into our Barisan Nasional manifesto," he said on the sidelines of the assembly today.
The proposal was introduced yesterday as part of Umno's
long-term vision
for the country ahead of the centenary of independence.
Zahid had said that the agenda would be pursued if Umno, BN, and their political allies return to power in Putrajaya.
It focuses on eight key initiatives aimed at creating wealth, developing human capital, widening ownership, improving wellbeing, strengthening resilience, caring for the people, restoring trust, and protecting national interests.
Commenting on the agenda, Zambry said it outlined efforts to strengthen the country's position in facing current and emerging challenges while ensuring peace, stability and prosperity.
"For example, there is the geopolitical challenge. We know that the world is becoming increasingly threatened and unstable, so we need careful planning to ensure that Malaysia remains peaceful and prosperous.
"That is what we need to do," he said.
He said Umno and BN's long experience in governing the country should be reflected in how the party approaches political and national issues.
"When we talk about politics, at the same time we must think about the country. Do not forget that.
"That is what we have established and fought for all this while. There may be shortcomings and political issues, but the most important thing is that this party, which is 80 years old, must look ahead to ensure Malaysia remains peaceful and stable," he said.
Zambry added that state delegates were expected to raise local issues during the assembly alongside national and party matters, noting that such discussions and requests for targeted attention were a standard part of deliberations.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Ministry monitoring haze impact on Malaysian students in Indonesia
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Higher Education Ministry is monitoring the prolonged haze in Indonesia to ensure the safety of thousands of Malaysian students studying there, says Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abdul Kadir.
The higher education minister said officials from Education Malaysia Global Services (EMGS), a company under the ministry, were tracking air quality across key regions, including Sumatra, Java and Sulawesi.
"So far, we have yet to receive reports indicating a severe impact, as conditions vary depending on the location of the respective universities," he told reporters at the 2026 Umno General Assembly.
"If the universities face serious problems, they may close, which would affect our students," he said, adding that EMGS officials had been directed to provide updates.
Indonesia has been experiencing prolonged haze, with several regions recording deteriorating air quality.
Separately, Mount Anak Krakatau erupted on Sept 5, producing a fountain of lava and booming sounds heard hundreds of kilometres away.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Parliament Open Day platform to bring democratic institution closer to people - Speaker
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysia Parliament Open Day 2026, being held today and tomorrow, serves as a platform to bring the institution closer to the people, while providing the public with an opportunity to see and understand the functions and processes taking place in the 'house of democracy'.
Dewan Rakyat Speaker Tan Sri Dr Johari Abdul said the public's interest in understanding the role of the institution could be seen among visitors who arrived as early as 7.30am, including visitors from abroad.
"People can come and see, not only the Parliament building but also what goes on inside Parliament. Two years ago, we had 10,000 visitors (over two days), but I think today (alone) there may be 10,000," he told reporters at the Malaysia Parliament Open Day 2026 today.
The two-day programme is being held in conjunction with the 67th anniversary of Parliament and National Month, featuring various activities including exhibitions, sales, sports competitions, pocket talks, film screenings by the National Film Development Corporation Malaysia (Finas) and stage performances.
Also present were Dewan Negara president Datuk Awang Bemee Awang Ali Basah, Dewan Negara Secretary Muhd Sujairi Abdullah and Dewan Rakyat Secretary Dr Nizam Mydin Bacha Mydin.
Meanwhile, Chief Administrator of the Malaysia Parliament Datuk Dr Ahmad Husaini Abdul Rahman said the concept of "bringing Parliament closer to the people" was not merely about bringing more visitors to the historic building, but was rooted in the principle that democratic institutions must always remain close to the people.
He said the people had the right to understand how Parliament functions, as the strength of the institution also depends on the extent to which the people appreciate, trust and feel that Parliament belongs to them.
"Institutional reform efforts must also not stop at the legal, structural or administrative aspects alone. Instead, the changes made must be felt by the people," he said.
For visitor Athirah Amalin Ahmad Daud, 28, the visit to Parliament gave her an opportunity to experience the atmosphere inside the institution while gaining a closer understanding of its functions.
"It is really exciting because all this while, I have only seen it on television, so being able to come inside myself is truly thrilling," said the civil servant.
Another visitor, Amir Haikal Mohd Firdaus, 23, hoped that programmes like this would continue so that more people would have the opportunity to get to know Parliament better.
"I hope programmes like this will be held regularly because many people may never have entered Parliament. When we come ourselves, we understand it better and feel closer to the institution," said the student of a public institution of higher learning.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Sarawak govt leaves heli crash probe to CAAM, says state minister
Article:
MIRI: The Sarawak government is leaving the investigation into the Flying Doctor Service (FDS) helicopter crash near Long Lellang, Ulu Baram, to the Civil Aviation Authority of Malaysia (CAAM).
Sarawak Transport Minister Datuk Seri Lee Kim Shin said the state government had obtained information on the flight operation upon receiving news of the crash.
He said the priority at the time was to ensure the rescue operation and recovery of the victims were carried out as quickly as possible, while the cause of the crash should be left to the authorities responsible for conducting the investigation.
"Every accident, whether involving an aircraft or helicopter, has standard operating procedures (SOPs). So, let us wait for the investigation to be conducted professionally and in accordance with the law," he said when met today.
He said it was inappropriate for any party to make various claims, assumptions or unverified comments about the cause of the crash, as the official report should be used as a reference before any conclusions are drawn.
He said the state government was still awaiting approval from Malaysia Airports and CAAM to resume flight operations at Long Lellang Airport.
"There was a proposal to resume operations on Sept 12 (today), but the final decision still depends on the notice and approval from the aviation authorities and airport management.
"We will wait for the announcement from Malaysia Airports and CAAM. They will issue the notice, and the approval will come from the authorities responsible," he said.
He said the Sarawak government would seek reports from CAAM and relevant agencies before taking further steps to improve flight safety, especially for flights to remote areas.
Meanwhile, he said the FDS was crucial in providing medical access to people in Sarawak's remote and rural areas.
"This is indeed a necessity for our people living in remote and rural areas. We have been operating the Flying Doctor Service in Sarawak for a long time," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Umno Youth seeks role in drafting BN manifesto for GE16
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Umno Youth wants a direct role in preparing the Barisan Nasional (BN) manifesto for the 16th General Election (GE16), particularly on issues affecting younger Malaysians.
Negri Sembilan Umno Youth chief Mohamad Fadil Md Zain said the voices of young Malaysians must be reflected in the BN manifesto after various issues affecting the people were raised during the assembly.
He said about 80 per cent of the issues discussed by Umno Youth at the assembly concerned matters affecting the people, while 20 per cent focused on politics.
"President, we have discussed various issues concerning young people. Some have raised education and economic issues, while Umno Youth also held Roundtable Dialogue 3.0 to bring together various groups, including professionals and youth associations, to hear their views on what young people want.
"Therefore, we ask that Umno Youth and Puteri Umno be involved in preparing the manifesto because the involvement of young people will help ensure Umno-BN secures a strong victory in the coming general election.
"Do not talk about young people without involving young people. Do not build a manifesto for the younger generation without giving them space to shape it.
"GE16 must be the point at which the voices of Umno Youth and Puteri are translated into policies, and the aspirations of voters are translated into BN's offer," he said while debating the president's policy speech at the 2026 Umno General Assembly here today.
Mohamad Fadil also urged BN component parties MCA and MIC not to fear ongoing efforts to explore cooperation between Umno and Pas.
He said such cooperation would not weaken the component parties but could instead strengthen their position.
"The experience in Negri Sembilan proves that such cooperation does not weaken the position of component parties. In fact, MCA won two seats in the last state election after previously having none.
"MCA's victory in taking a seat previously held by DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke is proof that BN can strengthen its position through cooperation and joint efforts.
"You do not need to fear this unity. You do not need to fear this cooperation. We have already proven in Negri Sembilan that MCA went from having no seats to winning two," he said.
Mohamad Fadil also urged Umno to be wise in choosing its political partners amid the country's changing political landscape to ensure the interests of the party and its members remained protected.
He said the decision to work with Pas in Negri Sembilan should be viewed maturely and should not cause concern among BN component parties.
"To Pas, we remind you and ask that you do not make us go into panic again," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Captain Zainol Afiq's remains expected to be buried in Senawang tomorrow
Article:
SEREMBAN: The remains of Flying Doctor Service (FDS) helicopter crash victim Captain Zainol Afiq Bee Sham are expected to be buried in Senawang tomorrow.
His father, Bee Sham Ahmad, 59, said the family was currently waiting for the deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) test results after samples were taken when they arrived in Miri on Wednesday.
"We were informed that the DNA results would be available today, but we do not know what time.
"If everything is settled, the remains will be brought home tomorrow. All preparations have been made," he said when contacted today.
He said the remains would be taken directly to Masjid Bandar Baru Senawang, Senawang, before being buried at Forest Height Muslim cemetery, Senawang.
It was reported that the DNA results of the five victims of the FDS helicopter crash in Long Lellang, near Miri, Sarawak, had been obtained and the remains would be handed over to their next of kin today.
The remains would be handed over to the victims' families after all relevant documentation had been completed.
The
crash on Tuesday
claimed the lives of all five people aboard the BO-105 helicopter operated by Layang-Layang Aerospace after it crashed near the end of the Long Lellang STOLport runway at about 3.40pm.
Medical assistant Alexson Adit Henry, 31; nurses Jessie Paya Jok, 44, and Debra Moset, 40; pilot Zainol Afiq, 30; and medical officer Dr Ainul Baraah Kamaruddin, 33, were reported killed in the incident.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: [UPDATED] Assets of second pilot linked to arrested Malaysia Airlines pilot frozen
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Police have frozen bank accounts and financial assets linked to a second pilot arrested over the seizure of RM45 million worth of drugs from a Malaysia Airlines pilot in Indonesia in July.
Narcotics Crime Investigation Department (NCID) director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said the second pilot, who is suspected of acting as a go-between for the Malaysia Airlines pilot and a drug syndicate, will be held for 60 days under the Dangerous Drugs (Special Preventive Measures) Act.
Hussein added that investigators are now scrutinising the pilot's bank accounts and other financial records linked to him.
However, he declined to reveal the amount of money found in the pilot's bank accounts.
"He (second pilot) is part of the syndicate involved in the flow of money obtained from the sale of drugs.
"He played a role in helping the co-pilot receive the money and transfer it," Hussein said.
He said assisting those involved in drug trafficking, including by receiving proceeds or allowing bank accounts to be used, would be treated as involvement in drug trafficking and dealt with under drug laws.
"We are not holding him under Section 39B of the Dangerous Drugs Act, but have instead detained him under special preventive measures for 60 days," he said.
Hussein added that the detention began on the day of the pilot's arrest.
He said the case would subsequently be referred to the Advisory Board for a decision on whether the suspect should be detained for a further two years.
Earlier this week, police
arrested
the second pilot over suspected links to the drug-smuggling syndicate.
This followed the arrest of a Malaysia Airlines second officer who was detained with drugs worth about RM45 million at Jakarta's Soekarno-Hatta International Airport.
The Malaysian was caught with 15 packets containing about 70,000 capsules suspected to contain ecstasy and methamphetamine, weighing about 25kg and estimated to be worth RM45 million.
The latest suspect, a Malaysian in his 30s, was arrested in the Klang Valley on Sept 7, bringing the number of people arrested locally in connection with the case to seven.
The others
arrested
are six Malaysian men aged between 23 and 50.
Police believe the six acted as suppliers and transporters for the pilot and occupied both "upline" and "downline" roles within the drug distribution network.
They were subsequently detained under the Dangerous Drugs (Special Preventive Measures) Act.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malaysia to investigate 30 citizens detained in Indonesia over online scams
Article:
PEKAN: Malaysia will conduct an investigation following the detention of 30 Malaysians suspected of being involved in online scam activities in Pontianak, West Kalimantan, Indonesia.
Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said the country's authorities would take appropriate action regarding the matter.
"The usual practice is for the Indonesian authorities to contact our police force to allow us to conduct an investigation from our perspective.
"The purpose is to establish whether this was an operation involving only these 30 people acting independently or whether they were part of a more organised syndicate.
"The information obtained will enable us to formulate a plan for further action," he said at a press conference after launcging the 2026 Madani Adopted Village and School by the Immigration Department at SK Nenasi today.
It was reported that Indonesian authorities detained 30 Malaysians and a Taiwanese national at a hotel at about 11.15am on Tuesday following intelligence on suspicious activities involving foreigners.

Meanwhile, Saufiddin Nasution, who is aso Pakatan Harapan secretary-general, said the Madani government's focus was currently on prioritising issues affecting the people.
"We stil have until February 2028… there are many more things we can do by leveraging our position in the government, maintaining stability, managing the economy prudently and focusing on the welfare of the people.
"More than a year is ample time for us to focus on fulfilling our responsibilities as leaders and safeguarding the people's welfare. In my view, that is more important," he said.
He said this when asked to comment on calls for the 16th general election (GE16) to be held earlier, before the current parliamentary term expires.

Title: First bodies of Philippines ferry fire victims land as toll hits 35
Article:
PHILIPPINES: The bodies of passengers killed in a ferry fire off the Philippines arrived at a port near the resort town of Coron, Palawan on Saturday morning, as the country's coast guard warned the death toll of 35 would grow.
AFP watched tents being set up to accept 30 bodies brought from the M/V June Aster, which ran aground near the tourist hotspot after a fire erupted Wednesday evening and tore through the vessel "in seconds."
Coast guard spokeswoman Noemie Cayabyab told a Saturday press conference the remains would be turned over to police forensic investigators for "proper disposition and identification" before allowing local authorities to inform family members.
"Currently, we are focused on the retrieval, and after that we will proceed with the investigation," she said, confirming the bodies had been found in the ship's economy accommodation area.
Police investigators were seen arriving at the port shortly after the press conference ended.
Asked how many bodies remained aboard the ship, she said authorities would provide an update later in the day.
Cayabyab told AFP on Friday evening that the first transfer had been capped at 30 bodies due to the capacity of the patrol vessel transporting them and that additional cadavers remained on the ferry.
Five others had been confirmed dead in the immediate wake of the fire.
Photos released by the coast guard showed rows of body bags being placed into a small ship alongside men in hazmat suits.
Thirty passengers and 13 crew have so far been rescued, while 54 people remain unaccounted for.
On Friday, Cayabyab had told a radio station the fire had begun in the cargo hold, then tore through the ship within seconds.
"From the time that they heard the loud explosion, the appearance of smoke, and then fire. It spread very quickly," she said of survivors' accounts.
"Everything happened in seconds," she said, adding that those who made it off the ship had not even had time to put on life jackets.
LOST HOPE
Myra Cabilan told AFP she had flown to Coron to find her missing brother, 40-year-old Rammel Gonzaga, who had taken the ferry from Manila on a business trip with his brother-in-law.
"His wife had just given birth a month ago. He was so happy he was given a daughter," Cabilan said, fighting back tears.
"At dawn, I still believed he survived. But he's still missing. I have lost hope."
Hundreds of people desperate for news about the incident have taken to leaving comments on the Facebook page of a local mayor, searching for relatives, friends and even a dog.
The ferry's manifest listed 134 crew and passengers, but two had not boarded, according to the coast guard. The ferry was also carrying goods, an electric vehicle, a pickup truck, and motorcycles.
The archipelago nation of 116 million has a long history of disasters involving the inter-island ferries that ply its seas.
Many rely on cheap and poorly regulated boats and ships for transport between the country's more than 7,000 islands, despite regular accidents.
In January, a triple-decker ferry carrying more than 340 people sank off the southern Philippines, killing at least 52 people.
The M/V Trisha Kerstin 3 sank along nearly the same route where 31 people died in 2023 after a fire broke out aboard the Lady Mary Joy 3 ferry.
On Thursday, the company that owns the M/V June Aster, Atienza Interisland Ferries Inc, said it was fully cooperating with the investigation.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: GE16 should be held early as government has entered 'election period', says Asyraf
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Umno believes the 16th General Election (GE16) should be brought forward as the current government's term has entered what it calls the "election period".
Umno secretary-general Datuk Seri Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki said the "election period" referred to the period after three years of a government's administration, when an election could be held although Parliament's maximum five-year term had not yet ended.
"From Umno's perspective, as we saw from the debates among delegates, we have reached the election period.
"The five-year term has not yet ended."The election period means any time after three years is a period in which an election can be held," he said after visiting the media centre for the 2026 Umno General Assembly.
Asyraf said Umno also believed that any major plans the party intended to implement or offer to the people should first receive a clear mandate from voters, particularly when they involved major national agendas.
He said the view had been echoed by delegates not only at the Umno General Assembly but also during the party's wing meetings.
"For Umno, as mentioned by the president (Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi) and also by delegates, not only at the Umno General Assembly but also at the party wings, as a government or a responsible political party, any major plans we want to carry out or offer to the people should appropriately be put to the people for a mandate," he said.
He said a similar situation had occurred during the Johor election, which was held after the state government had been in power for four years and one month.
At the time, he said, the state government had put forward a major 10-year plan under the "Johor Maju Johor" vision, which required a clear mandate from voters.
"It cannot be done simply at our own discretion. It must receive a clear mandate from the people," he said.
Yesterday, Zahid, who is also deputy prime minister, said Umno wanted GE16 to be brought forward so the party could seek a fresh mandate from voters to lead the country.
The Umno president said GE16 would be a defining point for the party to return to national leadership rather than remain merely a supporting component of the government.

Title: Too early to say if BN will continue with PH after GE16, says Asyraf
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: It is too early to say whether Barisan Nasional (BN) will continue cooperating with Pakatan Harapan (PH) after the 16th General Election (GE16), said Umno secretary-general Datuk Dr Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki.
He said formal negotiations had yet to begin and would only be held after Parliament was dissolved.
"It is premature to comment because negotiations have not even begun. As the president said, wait until Parliament is dissolved. Only then will negotiations begin," he told reporters after the 2026 Umno General Assembly here today.
Asyraf said the same approach was taken during the Johor and Negri Sembilan elections, where negotiations only began after the respective state assemblies were dissolved.
He said Umno's position on future political cooperation would depend on the outcome of negotiations and the political landscape at the time.
His remarks come amid calls within Umno for closer political cooperation with Pas ahead of GE16, including through the proposed Tafahum Siyasi, or political understanding.
Several delegates at the assembly also called for greater understanding between Umno and Pas, while Umno president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi had hinted at possible cooperation between the two parties by saying, "when blue meets green, the colours will surely change."
Asyraf said the current Unity Government remained intact and there was no attempt to change the administration before the next election.
He said Umno remained committed to political stability until Parliament was dissolved and the people were given the opportunity to determine the country's next government.
"The most important thing is that the president has indicated, and the delegates have also indicated, that the people should make the decision and the mandate should be given to the people," he said.

Title: 4,646 domestic violence cases recorded from January to July
Article:
JOHOR BARU: A total of 4,646 domestic violence cases were recorded nationwide from January to July this year, said Deputy Women, Family and Community Development Minister Lim Hui Ying.
Lim said this situation served as an important reminder that prevention efforts, early intervention and access to assistance channels must be continuously strengthened through initiatives by the Women's Development Department.
She said Johor recorded 823 cases, compared with 518 cases reported during the same period in 2025.
"Domestic violence does not only involve physical abuse, but can also take the form of emotional, psychological, sexual and financial abuse, including controlling a person's movements and relationships, which now also extends into the digital space.
"It often begins with behaviour that is perceived as normal, such as excessive control, threats or insults. Therefore, society needs to be alert to the early warning signs before the situation becomes more serious," she said.
​
She said this when officiating the Aku Wanita @ Domestic Violence (KRT) Well-being Advocacy Programme and the 2026 Johor PRISMAnita Open Day organised by the department in Seri Alam today.
In an effort to ensure women have faster and more systematic access to assistance, the Women, Family and Community Development Ministry has also provided PRISMAnita, which stands for Referral, Intervention, Support, Information and Advocacy for Women.
"PRISMAnita was launched by the prime minister on March 10 this year to connect women with government services and relevant agencies in a faster, more organised and customer-friendly manner.
"As of August, 117 clients had received services through PRISMAnita @ PPWN nationwide, while in Johor, this facility can be accessed through the Johor Women's Development Office," she said.
Those need assistance or wish to lodge a complaint are urged to contact the 24-hour Talian Kasih hotline at 15999, WhatsApp at 019-2615999, or visit the Johor Women's Development Office or the nearest police station.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Umno wants federal administration referred to as unity government
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Umno wants the current administration to continue being referred to as the Malaysia Unity Government instead of Malaysia Madani, its secretary-general Datuk Dr Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki said.
Asyraf said Umno had no issue with the Malaysia Madani concept, but stressed that the government should adhere to the terms of the agreement signed by the parties that formed it.
"Using the war cry and the Madani concept is not a problem. But when the Malaysia Madani Government is highlighted instead of the Malaysia Unity Government as agreed, that is the first issue.
"The agreement on the formation of the government clearly states that it must be called the Malaysia Unity Government," he told reporters when visiting the media centre for the 2026 Umno General Assembly here today.
Asyraf said the agreement involved 18 parties, meaning the administration was not a government belonging to a single political party.
"When Datuk Seri Anwar took the oath of office, an agreement involving 18 parties was formalised. It was called the Agreement on the Formation of the Malaysia Unity Government.
"This means the government is not a one-party government. The prime minister must always consult all the parties that make up the government," he said.
He said the arrangement differed from previous governments formed with a single party holding an outright majority.
"When it is a unity government, consultation must be made with all the respective parties," he said.
He said the use of the Malaysia Unity Government label was important to ensure all coalition partners remained involved in decisions affecting the administration.
Asyraf also rejected suggestions that Umno and Barisan Nasional had betrayed their coalition partners, saying the agreement remained in force until the next election.
"We have never betrayed anyone. Our agreement only applies until the election," he said.
He said political parties would be free to determine their respective alliances once Parliament or the state assemblies were dissolved.
