Title: Three cars buried under rubble as fence wall collapses in Seremban
Article:
SEREMBAN: A homeowner was jolted awake by a loud, thunder-like sound early this morning, only to discover that a fence wall under construction had collapsed and damaged three cars.
The incident occurred at about 3am, following heavy rain, with the collapsed structure bringing down concrete blocks onto the vehicles and road.
V. Tiagarajan, 43, said he was asleep when he heard the loud noise, followed by the sound of the collapse.
"I rushed out of the house to see what had happened. It turned out that the side section of my fence wall, which was still under construction, had completely collapsed and fallen onto three cars belonging to my neighbours parked outside.
"Concrete blocks were scattered on the cars and the road. The vehicles damaged were a Toyota Vios, Perodua Viva and Proton Persona," he said when met today.
He said construction of the boundary wall began about a month ago and was expected to be completed in another two weeks.
"I have informed the contractor about the incident and he has lodged a police report. He also said he would rebuild the wall.
"However, I am still worried because three cars belonging to my neighbours were damaged, although I did not suffer any property losses myself.
"Thankfully, no one was injured or killed, although the extent of the collapse was quite frightening.
"I cannot blame the contractor as the incident was caused by ground movement. It is the rainy season now, so that may have been a contributing factor," he said.
Meanwhile, vehicle owner May Lim, 58, said she was awakened by her child's car alarm.
"My child tried to switch it off, but to no avail. When we looked outside, we saw that the wall had collapsed onto my child's Toyota Vios and the Perodua Viva, which were parked outside the house," she said.
May said she accepted what had happened, saying her neighbour was prepared to take responsibility.
"Usually, the car is parked in our parking area. But this time, it was parked outside, and we never expected this to happen," she said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Mother's home-cooked meal left untouched after son dies in Johor crash
Article:
BATU PAHAT: A mother's last home-cooked meal for her son remained untouched after he was killed when his motorcycle was struck by a lorry near his workplace.
The victim's mother, Samsiah Kassan, 67, said she had prepared 'sambal ayam' for her youngest son, Mohamad Shahrul Azizi Sa'adon, 29, to take to work.
"He did not get to eat the sambal chicken I packed for him.
"That was the last meal I cooked for him before I found out that he had died in the accident," she said when met at her home in Kampung Parit Simpan, Senggarang, today.
The accident occurred yesterday at 7.30am, near the factory where the victim worked.
Samsiah said her youngest of four children had eaten the breakfast she prepared before leaving home for work as usual.
"Yesterday, I felt like cooking for him, so I prepared sambal chicken.
"I packed it in a container for him to take to work.
"On the day of the incident, he left home as usual. Not long afterwards, I received a call from a man informing me that my son had been involved in an accident.
"My body started shaking as I could not believe the news I had just received," she said.
Meanwhile, Batu Pahat police chief Assistant Commissioner Shahrulanuar Mushaddat Abdullah Sani said the accident occurred at Kilometre 116 of Jalan Johor Bahru-Melaka at about 7.30am.
He said the victim was riding from Senggarang towards Tanjung Laboh when the accident occurred.
"The motorcycle was involved in an accident with a lorry travelling in the opposite direction that is believed to have lost control.
"The 29-year-old victim suffered severe injuries to his head and legs and was pronounced dead at the scene.
"The 47-year-old lorry driver sustained injuries to his hip," he said.
The case is being investigated under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987 for causing death by reckless or dangerous driving, which carries a maximum prison sentence of 10 years and a fine of up to RM50,000 upon conviction.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Umno sets up committee to explore cooperation with Pas
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Umno will form a negotiation committee to handle possible political cooperation with Pas, as calls grow within the party for closer ties with the Islamist party.
Umno secretary-general Datuk Dr Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki said the committee would be established by the party leadership following views expressed by delegates at the 2026 Umno general assembly.
"A negotiation committee will be formed by the party leadership," he told reporters after the 2026 Umno general assembly today.
Asyraf said Umno had previously held negotiations with both Pas and Perikatan Nasional (PN) during past elections.
However, he said views expressed by delegates at this year's assembly showed a growing preference for direct engagement with the Pas leadership rather than negotiations with PN as a whole.
"As in previous elections, we have held negotiations with Pas and Perikatan Nasional.
"But if we look at the debates and views expressed by delegates, there is a tendency for us to focus on negotiations with the Pas leadership rather than looking at PN as a whole," he said.
He said the party leadership would take into account the views expressed by delegates when determining the direction of future political cooperation.
He said the formation of the committee was an internal move to prepare Umno for any discussions and did not mean that formal negotiations with Pas had already started.
He said the timing and scope of any talks would depend on the political situation and decisions by the party leadership.
Any cooperation would have to take into account Umno's interests and the broader political landscape, Asyraf said.
The move comes after several Umno leaders and delegates used the assembly to call for greater political understanding with Pas, including through the Tafahum Siyasi concept and the proposed Grand Coalition.
Umno president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi had also hinted at
possible closer cooperation
with Pas, saying "when blue meets green, the colours will surely change" in his policy speech.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Modi calls for removal of 10 key BRICS trade barriers
Article:
NEW DELHI: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi has urged BRICS member countries to remove 10 major trade barriers as India seeks to position itself as a bridge between the bloc and the global economy.
Speaking at the BRICS Business Forum, Modi called on the BRICS Business Council to prepare a report outlining ways to eliminate the 10 key trade barriers as the 11-nation bloc of emerging economies enters its 20th year.
"Can we support 100 BRICS startups each year to expand into other BRICS markets?
"Can we develop 1,000 new partnerships among our businesses? We should review our progress annually based on these three benchmarks," he said.
Modi said India has signed Free Trade Agreements (FTAs) with nearly 40 countries since 2014.
"Our approach within BRICS is the same: reducing barriers and expanding opportunities for business. Therefore, under India's chairmanship, we have established new cooperation networks in areas such as agriculture, healthcare, skills and smart grids.
"To connect startups and small and medium enterprises (SMEs) with markets and financing, we have launched initiatives such as the BRICS Incubator Network, the BRICS MSME Portal and the BRICS Startup Innovation Fund.
"You can all benefit from these cooperation frameworks and further enhance investment and talent exchanges among our countries," he said.
Modi said India is witnessing a startup revolution, emerging as a hub for global solutions with more than 200,000 startups and over 120 unicorns.
"Our startups are transforming the education and healthcare sectors through artificial intelligence (AI), working on green hydrogen and batteries, and exploring new frontiers in defence and space.
"Now, through BRICS as well, we must bring these world-class innovations to the global market," he said.
The BRICS Business Forum is part of the agenda for the 18th BRICS Leaders' Summit, which will also be attended by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
BRICS nations account for 50 per cent of the world's population, 40 per cent of global gross domestic product (GDP) and more than 25 per cent of global trade.
Malaysia is India's third-largest trading partner in Asean and ranks as the 31st-largest investor in India, with foreign direct investment (FDI) totalling US$1.34 billion from April 2000 to March 2026.
Around 70 to 80 Malaysian companies, including joint-venture firms, operate in India across sectors such as infrastructure, healthcare, telecommunications, oil and gas, power generation, automotive, fast-moving consumer goods (FMCG), tourism and human resources, with projects collectively valued at more than US$4 billion.
Overall Malaysian investment in India, including capital routed through third countries, is estimated at around US$3.3 billion, while announced investments exceed US$8.6 billion, primarily in renewable energy, green hydrogen, green ammonia and infrastructure.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: PH ready to contest all Melaka state seats if necessary, says Adam Adli
Article:
MELAKA: Pakatan Harapan is ready to contest all 28 seats in the upcoming Melaka election if necessary.
Acting Melaka PKR chief Adam Adli Abd Halim said this when asked about the coalition's preparedness for the polls amid reports of planned talks between PH and Barisan Nasional, which rules the state with a two-thirds majority.
"We must always be prepared because whether to negotiate or not is a choice, and every party has the right to decide.
"Contesting all seats will not be an issue for us, as we have done so before," he said on the sidelines of the Kampung Angkat Madani programme in Kampung Sungai Putat.
Previously, Melaka Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh said BN would only begin
negotiations
after the dissolution of the Melaka State Assembly, which he
hinted
would happen soon.
Adam Adli said Melaka PH wanted the upcoming polls to be a healthy contest and not a source of division.
"Elections should not affect harmony in the state," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Police still hunting robbers behind RM2.9mil Jalan Ampang condo heist
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Police are still hunting for the armed robbers who broke into a condominium unit on Jalan Ampang on Monday and made off with RM2.9 million in cash and valuables.
Wangsa Maju police chief Assistant Commissioner Annas Sulaiman said there were no new developments at the moment.
"The investigation is ongoing, so give us some time to work," he said when contacted.
It was reported earlier that the 28-year-old victim, a Chinese national, suffered losses amounting to RM2.9 million after a group of knife-wielding men broke into his home on Monday afternoon.
The victim lodged a police report the same evening.
Police are also probing the possibility of an inside job, given the tight security at the condominium. Statements have been taken from 12 witnesses.
The case is being investigated under Sections 395 and 397 of the Penal Code for gang robbery and gang robbery with a deadly weapon.
The offences are punishable by a maximum 20-year jail term and caning.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Common for parties to seek general election after three years, says Tok Mat
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: It is common for political parties to seek a fresh mandate from voters after a government had been in power for three years, Umno deputy president Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan said.
Speaking on the sidelines of the 2026 Umno General Assembly here today, he said the current government had now been in power for more than three years.
"Now it has been more than three years. Typically, the mood for holding an election comes after three years.
"Whether it should be held or not is up to them.
"Political parties will always want to seek a fresh mandate from the people," he said.
Mohamad said Umno, as one of the political parties with a stake in the country's political landscape, also wanted to secure a fresh mandate from its supporters and voters.
Yesterday, Umno president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi
declared
an all-out war against the party's political rivals when he reiterated his call for an early 16th General Election (GE16).
He said the call reflected the wishes of the people rather than a demand or hope from the party.
Meanwhile, on Kedah Umno information chief Datuk Shaiful Hazizy Zainol Abidin's
remark
that the state chapter would begin political cooperation talks with Pas, but not Perikatan Nasional (PN), Mohamad said any discussions at the state level should be brought to the attention of the party headquarters.
"Let them hold whatever discussions they want at the state level. Whatever discussions they have, they need to bring them to the attention of the headquarters.
"When the time comes, the top leadership will review all the negotiations and discussions that have taken place because, as I mentioned, there is no one-size-fits-all approach.
"We want to diversify because the political situation in the
country
is no longer uniform. So, we cannot use one formula that can be applied to every state," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Justice delayed must still be justice delivered — Syed Mohammed Idid
Article:
SEPTEMBER 12 — The Malaysian Bar President Anand Raj’s statement on the circumstances surrounding my father, Dato’ Syed Ahmad Idid, struck me not merely as a son, but as a communications practitioner and someone increasingly immersed in the responsibilities of governance.
Thirty years is a long time.
But is it ever too late to right a wrong?
I do not believe so.
Justice must not only be seen to be done. Justice must be done — and done well.
Justice may take time. Institutions may change. Governments change. Leaders come and go.
Records gather dust.
But justice must eventually arrive, and when it does, it must be delivered with courage and clarity.
The Malaysian Bar has described what happened to my father as a “miscarriage of justice” and called upon the Government to restore his full pension, including arrears. More importantly, its statement makes a larger point: integrity must not be punished.
A statue of the scales of justice, symbolising the pursuit of fairness and accountability, which are themes at the heart of this opinion article on justice delayed and institutional integrity. — Freepik pic
That principle travels far beyond the Judiciary.
It belongs equally in the boardroom.
As I deepen my own journey into corporate governance, I increasingly see a powerful parallel between judicial responsibility and fiduciary duty.
A judge carries the enormous responsibility of administering justice independently, without fear or favour.
A director carries a different but similarly solemn responsibility: to exercise independent judgement, act in good faith, discharge fiduciary duties and protect the interests and integrity of the organisation entrusted to his or her stewardship.
The institutions are different. The gravitas of their responsibilities is comparable.
Governance is therefore not simply about compliance, board papers, policies, risk registers and ticking the right boxes.
It is about conscience under pressure.
What happens when speaking up is inconvenient?
What happens when the person raising the uncomfortable question is the lone voice in the room?
What happens when protecting institutional reputation becomes confused with protecting individuals or preserving silence?
These are not theoretical governance questions. They go to the heart of institutional integrity.
Boards should understand this particularly well.
A healthy institution does not punish the person who raises a legitimate concern. It examines the concern. It protects the integrity of the process. It allows independent judgement to operate.
And when an institution discovers that something was wrong, good governance demands the courage to correct it.
Even years later.
Because the passage of time does not automatically convert a wrong into a right.
Nor should correcting an historical wrong be regarded as institutional weakness.
It can be one of the strongest demonstrations of institutional maturity.
That, to me, is the deeper significance of the Malaysian Bar President’s statement.
This is no longer simply about one retired judge, one pension or something that happened three decades ago.
It is about the kind of institutions Malaysia wants to build.
Institutions in which judges can act independently.
Boards can challenge management.
Employees can speak up.
Whistleblowers can raise legitimate concerns without destroying their careers.
And leaders have sufficient confidence in their institutions to acknowledge when something needs to be put right.
There is perhaps a governance lesson here for every director and every leader:
Never fear the uncomfortable truth more than you fear the consequences of ignoring it.
Justice may be delayed.
Accountability may take time.
But neither should carry an expiry date.
Because ultimately, whether in a courtroom or a boardroom, institutional trust rests on something remarkably simple:
Do what is right.
Do it without fear or favour.
And when something has gone wrong, have the courage to put it right.
* This is the personal opinion of the writer or publication and does not necessarily represent the views of Malay Mail.

Title: ‘We still have until February 2028’, Pakatan sec-gen says as GE16 chatter grows
Article:
PEKAN, Sept 12 — Pakatan Harapan secretary-general Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail today brushed aside calls for the 16th general election to be held earlier, saying the Madani government’s term only expires in February 2028.
Saifuddin Nasution was responding to questions from reporters after officiating the launch of the 2026 Madani Adopted Village and School by the Immigration Department at Sekolah Kebangsaan Nenasi here, national news agency
Bernama
reported.
“We still have until February 2028… there are many more things we can do by leveraging our position in the government, maintaining stability, managing the economy prudently and focusing on the welfare of the people,” he was quoted saying.
“More than a year is ample time for us to focus on fulfilling our responsibilities as leaders and safeguarding the people's welfare. In my view, that is more important,” he added.
Speculation over GE16’s timing has intensified in recent months, even though Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim's administration is not required to call the polls until Parliament automatically dissolves in December 2027, with an election to follow within 60 days after that.
Anwar is from the same party and coalition as Saifuddin Nasution.
Political analysts have floated several possible windows for an early dissolution, including the final quarter of 2026 to align with a cluster of state elections in Melaka, Sarawak and Johor, or shortly after Budget 2027 is tabled.
Some observers have also linked the timing to internal coalition dynamics that could trigger a chain of events leading to dissolution as early as February 2027.
Anwar has previously signalled that Parliament could be dissolved earlier than scheduled if coalition partners act in ways that threaten political stability — a remark made after Umno and the Barisan Nasional coalition it leads decided to contest solo in all Johor seats during that state’s own polls.
The Election Commission has said it remains fully prepared for any early dissolution of state assemblies or a snap GE16, amid the persistent speculation.

Title: Were the 30 Malaysians caught in Indonesia lone scammers, or something bigger? Home Ministry to dig deeper
Article:
PEKAN, Sept 12 — Malaysia will conduct an investigation following the detention of 30 Malaysians suspected of being involved in online scam activities in Pontianak, West Kalimantan, Indonesia.
Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said the country’s authorities would take appropriate action regarding the matter.
“The usual practice is for the Indonesian authorities to contact our police force to allow us to conduct an investigation from our perspective.
“The purpose is to establish whether this was an operation involving only these 30 individuals acting independently or whether they were part of a more organised syndicate. The information obtained will enable us to formulate a plan for further action,” he said.
He said this at a media conference after officiating the launch of the 2026 Madani Adopted Village and School by the Immigration Department at Sekolah Kebangsaan Nenasi here today.
It was reported that Indonesian authorities detained 30 Malaysians and a Taiwanese national at a hotel at about 11.15 am on Tuesday following intelligence on suspicious activities involving foreign nationals.
Meanwhile, Saifuddin Nasution, who is also Pakatan Harapan secretary-general, said the Madani Government’s focus was currently on prioritising issues affecting the people.
“We still have until February 2028… there are many more things we can do by leveraging our position in the government, maintaining stability, managing the economy prudently and focusing on the welfare of the people.
“More than a year is ample time for us to focus on fulfilling our responsibilities as leaders and safeguarding the people’s welfare. In my view, that is more important,” he said.
He said this when asked to comment on calls for the 16th General Election to be held earlier, before the current parliamentary term expires. — Bernama

Title: Anwar to Iran: Keep Hormuz open, choose diplomacy over conflict
Article:
NEW DELHI, Sept 12 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim expressed concern over the continued conflict and escalation across West Asia during a bilateral meeting with Iran President Masoud Pezeshkian today.
Anwar, who is here for the 18th BRICS Leaders’ Summit, reiterates the importance of maintaining the freedom and safety of maritime passage through the Strait of Hormuz in accordance with international law.
“Malaysia urged all parties to return to dialogue and diplomacy to resolve disputes and de-escalate the situation,” the prime minister said during a 30-minute meeting between the two leaders on the sidelines of the summit here.
Anwar, who is also finance minister, welcomed Putrajaya and Tehran’s long-standing diplomatic relations and reaffirmed cooperation on various fronts.
He also called on a continuation and expansion of trade and investment cooperation and opportunities, especially in energy, agriculture, palm oil, food security, halal, technology, and higher education. — Bernama

Title: Mission done, but not over: Smart team on way home as Nepal search continues
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 12 — The Special Malaysia Disaster Assistance and Rescue Team (Smart), which participated in the Humanitarian Assistance and Disaster Relief mission in Nepal, is expected to return home today or tomorrow, said Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan.
He stated that all equipment belonging to the team, such as drones, has been handed over to rescue teams in Nepal for use in search operations for flood victims in the country.
“Nepalese authorities do not intend (at this time) to announce the termination of search and rescue (SAR) operations, as there are still 5,000 people unaccounted for.
“The Smart team leader will provide a report and assess the next steps so that we do not make hasty decisions; if they (Nepal) require assistance from Malaysia, we can consider helping with the search or rescue operations,” he said.
Mohamad told reporters while visiting the Media Centre at the 2026 Umno General Assembly here today.
The Smart MAS01 team, participating in the Humanitarian Assistance and Disaster Relief mission to Nepal, arrived in the country via Tribhuvan International Airport, Kathmandu, on September 5.
The team, comprising 11 personnel and officers, departed for Nepal on a Royal Malaysian Air Force A400M aircraft from the RMAF Subang Air Base, carrying 12.4 tonnes of SAR equipment.
Meanwhile, Mohamad stated that the Malaysian Embassy in Kathmandu is in constant contact with the Nepalese government to obtain the latest information regarding the status of Malaysians reported missing in the tragedy.
He said this is to enable next-of-kin to handle matters such as insurance claims and other related issues.
“In Nepal, for anyone reported missing or unaccounted for, a death certificate can be issued after three years, whereas in Malaysia, it takes seven years.
“That is why we have asked the (Malaysian) embassy there to liaise with the (Nepalese) ministry to determine how next-of-kin can obtain documents confirming the status of the Malaysians who remain missing,” he said. — Bernama

Title: After Bandar Tasik Selatan PPR gets RM350,000 makeover, MP asks residents to ‘take good care’ for sake of kids and grandkids
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 12 — A total of RM350,000 has been allocated for road upgrading works at Pangsapuri Kos Rendah Bandar Tasik Selatan here under the 2026 Projek Mesra Rakyat initiative.
Bandar Tun Razak Member of Parliament Datuk Seri Dr Wan Azizah Wan Ismail said repair works on the lifts at the apartments would also be carried out soon to ensure residents’ comfort.
“Once upgraded, please take good care of these facilities. We must work together to develop and maintain them so that our children and grandchildren can also enjoy the benefits,” she said while officiating the Bandar Tun Razak Parliamentary Constituency Kenduri Rakyat Madani 2026 programme here today.
At the same event, the Prime Minister’s wife also launched a RM72,000 Flexi EV charging station comprising four electric vehicle charging units at the apartment complex.
She said the project was implemented in collaboration with the apartment’s management corporation, Leading Innovative Technologies & Systems Sdn Bhd and Pro Parking Sdn Bhd.
Dr Wan Azizah said the initiative demonstrated how collaboration among the community, management bodies and the private sector could deliver better facilities for residents.
She also urged residents to make full use of the available facilities and services while working together to address community issues.
Dr Wan Azizah also presented Ember AI tuition sponsorships to 10 Form Five students who will sit for the Sijil Pelajaran Malaysia examination this year.
She also stressed the need to ensure children receive adequate nutrition to support their growth, particularly amid the challenges of urban living.
The Special Kenduri Rakyat Madani satellite programme aims to foster closer ties between leaders, government agencies and the local community while bringing government information and services closer to the people.
More than 1,000 local residents attended the programme organised by the Information Department, which featured Jualan Rahmah and Jualan Agro Madani, as well as health check-ups, mammogram services and anaemia screenings. — Bernama

Title: Foreign Ministry seeks DNA samples of Nepal flood victims to identify missing Malaysians
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 12 — Malaysia is reportedly in talks with Nepal to have DNA samples from flood victims found during search-and-rescue operations sent here for matching against samples taken from relatives of Malaysians who remain missing, Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan said today.
According to
Utusan Malaysia
, Mohamad said the initiative was proposed because Nepalese authorities face shortages of facilities and equipment needed to identify victims.
“Send them here so it will be easier for us to carry out matching with close family members whose DNA samples have already been taken,” he was quoted as saying.
Mohamad reportedly said Malaysia was also considering sending DNA experts to Nepal, while the Malaysian Embassy in Kathmandu has asked Nepalese security authorities to forward samples already collected from recovered victims.
He said the proposal had been submitted to the Nepalese government and Malaysia was awaiting a response.
Mohamad said Malaysia is also discussing with Nepal ways to help families of missing Malaysians obtain documents needed for matters such as insurance claims.
At last count, 55 Malaysians remained missing following the August 26 floods and landslides in Nepal.

Title: Umno won’t ‘betray anyone’ or seek new PM before next general election, says Asyraf Wajdi
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 12 — Umno secretary-general Datuk Seri Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki today said the party would not seek to change the prime minister or form a new government before the next general election is called.
He said Umno remained committed to political stability and had yet to begin negotiations for the next general election.
“As long as the elections are not called, we will not ‘tebuk atap’ (form a backdoor government) or seek to change the prime minister,” he told reporters at a press conference on the sidelines of the 2026 Umno General Assembly today.
“We have not started negotiations for the next election. Talks will only begin after Parliament is dissolved, just as they did after the state legislative assemblies in Johor and Negri Sembilan were dissolved,” he said.
Asyraf Wajdi was responding to questions about remarks by Umno president Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi, who yesterday appeared to criticise Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim’s past election promise to rein in petrol prices within 24 hours and the flip-flop over the Budi95 fuel subsidy quota.
While the Umno-led Barisan Nasional (BN) sits with Pakatan Harapan in the federal government, it governs Negri Sembilan with Islamist party PAS.
Speculation over Umno strengthening political ties with PAS intensified after PAS secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan and several other senior party leaders attended the Umno General Assembly yesterday.
Asyraf Wajdi also refuted claims that Umno would be committing a “betrayal” by seeking political cooperation with other parties.
“Umno isn’t betraying anyone. The agreement (to form the unity government) is only applicable until the next general election is called.
“After that, all parties are free to choose their own directions. I don’t expect even Sabah and Sarawak to want to be dictated to on who they should cooperate with,” he said.

Title: Stop hunting for jobs, start creating them, minister tells TVET grads as 97pc find work
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Sept 12 — The Ministry of Youth and Sports (KBS) provides avenues and opportunities for graduates with disabilities, including those with autism, to enter the workforce, including the public service, after completing their studies at the Youth and Sports Skills Training Institutes (ILKBS).
Its Minister, Dr Mohammed Taufiq Johari, said the ministry maintained data on ILKBS graduates and alumni each year to track their career paths, with most securing opportunities in the industry, as well as in the private and public sectors.
“We (KBS) want to support this effort to ensure that the target of having at least one per cent of persons with disabilities in the public service is achieved.
“At Menara KBS itself, we provide opportunities for them to operate a cafe and provide services. That is one example,” he told reporters after attending the 21st ILKBS Convocation Ceremony 2026 here today.
Mohammed Taufiq said 4,155 graduates received their certificates at this year’s convocation after completing diploma, advanced certificate and skills certificate programmes in various fields offered by ILKBS, including 130 youths with disabilities and autism.
He said one of ILKBS’ advantages was that 20 per cent of the overall learning at its institutions focused on character development and identity, while the remaining 80 per cent centred on skills, including graduates’ participation in community programmes as a way of giving back to society.
He also welcomed the implementation of Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) 2.0, saying the ministry would continue to empower youth and sports skills training institutions, including through collaborations with industry players.
He said that, so far, 180 memoranda of understanding (MoUs) had been signed with various parties and industry players to bolster cooperation in TVET, including the automotive and electrical sectors, which were among those with high demand.
“We have active cooperation with industry players. The automotive and electrical fields have the highest demand, and we are also exploring more new industries that are growing rapidly. We want to ensure that we provide these spaces and opportunities to our students. So, the total number of 180 MoUs could increase,” he added.
Mohammed Taufiq also urged ILKBS graduates not to only target job opportunities domestically but to also look at the potential of overseas markets, including the Asean region, which has a population of around 700 million.
“Graduates need to keep pace with current developments, including artificial intelligence (AI) and digital technology, and should not merely seek employment but also be capable of creating jobs,” he said, adding that ILKBS currently recorded a graduate employability rate of 97 per cent.
Meanwhile, recipient of the ILKBS Overall Best Graduate Award, Muhammad Haffiz Rahim, described the recognition as a sweet moment that would remain etched in his mind, adding that he wanted to further develop his potential to make the most of his talents and repay his parents for their sacrifices.
The 25-year-old, the eldest of four siblings, completed a Diploma in Automotive Maintenance Engineering Technology at the National Youth Advanced Skills Institute (IKTBN) Temerloh, and said he aspired to go further by securing a job in the public sector, specifically with KBS.
Hailing from Bentong, Pahang, he said his success through the TVET pathway had also motivated him to share his experience and encourage his relatives to pursue the field, which he described as offering bright prospects in terms of employment opportunities.
“TVET is a very good field and has a bright future in terms of employment opportunities. If there is an opportunity, I hope to work with KBS, especially in managing programmes such as National Sports Day and National Youth Day,” he added. — Bernama
* Editor’s note: The initials KBS stands for Kementerian Belia dan Sukan in Malay while ILKBS stands for Institut Latihan Kemahiran Belia dan Sukan.

Title: Empty posts, crumbling clinics: Sarawak wants the power to fix its own healthcare
Article:
KUCHING, Sept 12 — Sarawak is pushing for regulatory powers under the Private Healthcare Facilities and Services Act 1998 (Act 586) to be decentralised to the state Health Department (JKNS), said Deputy Premier Datuk Amar Dr Sim Kui Hian.
He said the matter was among three key areas of Sarawak’s health autonomy that he raised on Friday’s Malaysia Agreement 1963 (MA63) Implementation Action Council meeting in Kota Kinabalu.
“The one that impacts most is the Private Healthcare Facilities and Services Act 1998 (Act 586),” he shared in his Facebook post.
He said the regulatory function should be decentralised to JKNS from the Ministry of Health (MOH), in line with the MOH White Paper and provisions under the Federal Constitution allowing such delegation of power.
Dr Sim also called for urgent action to address Sarawak’s shortage of health personnel, with 5,654 vacant posts currently under JKNS.
He said the vacancies accounted for 18 per cent of the state health workforce and staff were not only overworked but also facing burnout.
For the medium term, he proposed the creation of 11,000 posts across various categories to meet MOH staffing norms following an audit of seven Sarawak hospitals last year.
“There is no reason for Sarawak to be sub-standard in manpower,” he said.
On infrastructure, Dr Sim said Sarawak needed RM310 million to upgrade dilapidated Klinik Kesihatan (KK) facilities and RM8.45 billion for their redevelopment.
He said 160 of the state’s 271 KKs, or 66 per cent, were classified as dilapidated.
“There is no reason why Sarawak having more KK
daif
compared to the rest of Malaysia,” he said.
Dr Sim said health was among the more complex MA63 matters, involving 41 laws.
He said while some MA63 issues had been resolved, the remaining negotiations would be tougher as some involved constitutional amendments requiring approval at Cabinet and Parliament level and, in certain cases, the Conference of Rulers.
He said the negotiations must take into account the spirit of MA63, as well as the Cobbold Commission and Inter-Governmental Committee reports.
“MA63 is a journey. We shall move forward with courage, wisdom and the spirit of our founding fathers,” he said. — The Borneo Post
* Editor’s note: Daif in Malay, used in the quote above by Sarawak
Deputy Premier Datuk Dr Sim Kui Hian,
means dilapidated.

Title: Early morning blaze guts first floor of Kuching retail chain, no injuries reported
Article:
KUCHING, Sept 12 — A fire broke out at a retail chain near Jalan Tun Ahmad Zaidi Adruce here early on Saturday morning.
The Sarawak Fire and Rescue Department (better known locally as Bomba) dispatched firefighters from the Batu Lintang fire station after receiving a call at around 3.42am.
“The fire broke out on the first floor involving various goods. No victims were reported at the scene.
“The first floor was completely destroyed while the second floor was severely damaged.
“Firefighters managed to keep the fire under control at around 5.18am and overhaul works are being done,” Bomba said.
As of 7am, firefighters were still at the scene to extinguish the fire.
The firefighters were supported by a water tanker from the Tabuan Jaya fire station to facilitate firefighting efforts due to low water pressure from the fire hydrant. — The Borneo Post

Title: Lawyer denies govt forfeited funds in Abdul Azeez family’s Tabung Haji accounts
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 12 — A lawyer for former Tabung Haji (TH) chairman Datuk Seri Abdul Azeez Abdul Rahim has reportedly denied claims that the government forfeited RM18 million held in TH accounts belonging to his family members.
According to
New Straits Times
, Datuk Amer Hamzah Arshad also rejected claims that savings belonging to Azeez’s wife and children were linked to TH funds, saying such allegations — which were posted on social media — were not related to the criminal charge faced by his client.
He reportedly said in a press statement that Azeez was not charged with taking, misappropriating or misusing the RM193.5 million mentioned in the case for himself or his family.
Instead, Amer reportedly said the charge read out at the Sessions Court on September 8 alleged that Azeez used his position as TH chairman to obtain the chairmanship of Putrajaya Perdana Bhd, which brought benefits including annual remuneration, a vehicle and a permanent driver.
“The RM193.5 million mentioned in the charge is the value of TH’s investment in Putrajaya Perdana Bhd and not money alleged to have been given to, taken by or deposited into the personal accounts of our client or his family members,” Amer was quoted as saying.
He added that the family’s TH accounts had previously been investigated by the authorities, but the savings had never been forfeited by the government or found to be misappropriated TH funds or proceeds of illegal activities.
Amer also reportedly said the Royal Commission of Inquiry into TH had made no finding that Azeez had taken or misappropriated TH funds for himself or his family, adding that Azeez has pleaded not guilty to the charge.
He said Azeez and his family reserved the right to take legal action against anyone who published or spread false, misleading or defamatory statements over the matter.
The charge against Azeez relates to an alleged offence at a TH board meeting on August 25, 2014, and was framed under Section 23(1) of the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission Act 2009, which carries a maximum jail term of 20 years and a fine upon conviction.
His prosecution is among several cases involving former TH officials following the release in July of the Royal Commission of Inquiry report into the pilgrimage fund’s management, which flagged a number of problematic investments, including the Putrajaya Perdana deal.

Title: Sarawak dialysis patient’s rescue shows why the Flying Doctor Service matters
Article:
KUCHING, Sept 12 — When a helicopter crashed just 200 metres from her home in Long Lellang, Renai Iwat was not only confronted with the trauma of losing a vital link to medical care, but also another race against time.
The dialysis patient, who requires treatment three times a week, needed to return to Miri after the Long Lellang STOLport was closed following Tuesday’s tragic helicopter crash that claimed the lives of four medical personnel and a pilot.
Amid the grief and uncertainty, her family turned to the authorities for help.
Renai was eventually airlifted from Long Lellang to Miri Hospital on Thursday (Sept 10) by a Bomba helicopter, allowing her to resume the treatment on which she depends.
A family member who wished to remain anonymous said the family would remain deeply grateful to Deputy Minister in the Premier’s Department (Labour, Immigration and Project Monitoring) Datuk Gerawat Gala, Miri Division Resident Tuan Galong Luang and Bomba for making the evacuation possible.
She said Gerawat had personally raised the urgency of bringing Renai back to Miri because of her dialysis schedule and had insisted that arrangements be made for her evacuation.
“Although we are deeply saddened by the loss of the four medical personnel and pilot in the tragic helicopter incident, Renai’s case shows how important the Flying Doctor Service is to our rural communities,” she told
The Borneo Post
when contacted.
She said the family’s concern was heightened by the fact that Renai had been at home when the helicopter crashed nearby.
“It was an extremely difficult situation for her and for all of us,” she said.
She also thanked Miri Health Department head Dr P Raviwharmman Packierisamy for supporting the request for Renai’s medical evacuation.
According to her, Galong then made the formal request to Bomba for the evacuation from Long Lellang to Miri, while the Bomba director approved the use of its helicopter.
She expressed particular appreciation to the helicopter captain and crew who flew back to Long Lellang to bring Renai safely to Miri.
Renai Iwat seated aboard the Bomba helicopter en route to Miri Hospital, accompanied by rescue personnel after her successful medical evacuation from Long Lellang. — The Borneo Post pic
For Renai, the evacuation was more than simply getting home.
It meant returning to hospital for treatment she needs three times a week and being reunited with her family after an ordeal that unfolded dangerously close to home.
Renai is the widow of the late Pemanca Freddy Abun, who served the Kelabit community for more than five years.
For the family, Renai’s experience underscored the importance of air medical services to communities in Sarawak’s remote interior, where access to healthcare can depend on the ability to travel by air.
The family also extended their condolences to the families of those who lost their lives in the crash.
They said Renai’s safe evacuation was a powerful reminder that for people living in remote communities, air medical services are not a luxury but a lifeline.
And for one family, that lifeline brought a mother, wife and grandmother safely home. — The Borneo Post

Title: No special treatment in Peter Anthony’s release, says Prisons Department
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 12 — Malaysia’s Prisons Department said the release of former Sabah Infrastructure Minister Datuk Peter Anthony under the Licensed Prisoner Release Programme (PBSL) was granted after he met the required eligibility period and underwent the same screening and assessment process as other prisoners considered for the programme.
In a statement issued today, the department stressed that PBSL was not a cancellation, reduction or shortening of a court-imposed sentence.
“Prisoners granted PBSL continue to serve the remainder of their sentences, but do so in the community, subject to the conditions, regulations, supervision and monitoring of the Malaysian Prisons Department,” it said.
“To be considered for participation in PBSL, a prisoner must first meet the eligibility requirements, including having served at least one-third of the sentence. However, serving this minimum period does not automatically qualify a prisoner for release under PBSL,” it added.
Each candidate undergoes screening and assessment based on their conduct and character in prison, rehabilitation progress, participation in human development programmes, readiness to return to the community, family support, housing suitability, employment prospects and post-release monitoring needs.
At headquarters, applications are reviewed by a PBSL committee chaired by the Commissioner-General of Prisons and comprising senior officers and representatives from relevant agencies.
“Regarding the release of former Sabah Infrastructure Minister Datuk Peter Anthony, the Prisons Department stresses that consideration for his participation in PBSL was made after he reached the prescribed eligibility period and underwent the screening and assessment process applied to other candidates considered for the programme,” it said.
The department added that Anthony’s release did not mean that the remainder of his sentence had been waived. He would continue serving the balance of his sentence in the community and remain subject to the conditions, regulations and monitoring imposed throughout the period.
“An individual’s status is not a criterion that provides an advantage or exemption from the prescribed eligibility and assessment process,” the department added.
Peter Anthony was sentenced to three years in prison and fined RM50,000 after being convicted of falsifying documents linked to a Universiti Malaysia Sabah maintenance contract.
His conviction and sentence were upheld on appeal, and he began serving his sentence in March 2025 before being released under PBSL in March 2026.
MCA president Datuk Seri Wee Ka Siong accused Pakatan Harapan of applying double standards by demanding full sentences for high-profile offenders while remaining silent when former Sabah minister Peter Anthony was released on parole after serving about a year of his three-year sentence.

Title: DNA results of Long Lellang crash victims finally in, families set to receive remains
Article:
MIRI, Sept 12 — The DNA (deoxyribonucleic acid) test results for the five victims of the Flying Doctor Service (FDS) helicopter crash in Long Lellang in Baram have been obtained, and the remains will be handed over to the next of kin today, said Sarawak Police Commissioner Datuk Mohamad Zainal Abdullah.
“Today, once the documentation is completed, the remains will be handed over to the families,” he told Bernama when contacted.
Meanwhile, funeral arrangements are under way for three of the five victims, as their families prepare to bid their final farewells.
Medical assistant Alexson Adit Henry will be laid to rest at the Anglican Cemetery in Lambir following a funeral service at the Good Shepherd Church in Lutong at 9 am on Sept 15.
His sister, Annastasia Luyah, said in a funeral notice shared on her Facebook last night that a wake will be held on Sept 14 at their family residence at Taman Desa Senadin here.
The wake for staff nurse Jessie Paya Jok will be held at Taman Wang Lusut while the body of staff nurse Debra Moset will be brought home to Kampung Semadang in Padawan, Kuching, for a wake service. The burial dates have yet to be announced.
All five people on board the BO-105 helicopter operated by Layang-Layang Aerospace were killed after it crashed near the end of the Long Lellang STOLport runway at about 3.40 pm on Sept 8.
The other two who lost their lives were medical officer Dr Ainul Baraah Kamaruddin and pilot Captain Zainol Afiq Bee Sham.
Dr Ainul is expected to be laid to rest at the Sri Kedeper Muslim Cemetery in Kelantan, while Captain Zainol will be brought home to Negeri Sembilan for burial.
Yesterday Mohamad Zainal said post-mortem examinations on all five victims were completed at the Forensic Department of Miri Hospital on Thursday night and the DNA analysis was expected to be completed today. — Bernama

Title: Economy minister says Malaysia to deepen renewable energy, connectivity ties with Indonesia, Thailand
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 12 — Malaysia is committed to strengthening regional cooperation in the field of renewable energy and connectivity as an effort to expand economic opportunities at the sub-regional level of Asean, said Minister of Economy Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir.
He said that sub-regional approaches such as the Indonesia-Malaysia-Thailand Growth Triangle (IMT-GT) can strengthen the economic potential among member countries through the implementation of more structured and effective plans.
“At the Malaysian level, we acknowledge the implementation we have carried out for the blueprint until 2026, and at this moment, we are planning the next blueprint from 2027 to 2031 before moving towards the IMT-GT Vision 2036,” he said at a press conference while attending the 32nd IMT-GT Ministerial Meeting in Medan, Indonesia.
The meeting was held on Sept 10, under the chairmanship of Indonesian Coordinating Minister for Economic Affairs Airlangga Hartanto, and attended by Thailand’s Vice Minister for Office of the Prime Minister Dr Thanadit Raktabutr.
According to Akmal Nasrullah, one of the main focuses includes strengthening the renewable energy sector through initiatives such as the Asean Power Grid, as well as enhancing the level of physical connectivity between Malaysia, Indonesia, and Thailand.
He said that the close geographical proximity between Kuala Lumpur and Medan needs to be fully utilised to accelerate economic integration.
At the same time, Akmal Nasrullah also emphasised the importance of sustainability and digital agendas as new growth drivers, including expanding opportunities in the green economy in the sub-region.
He also expressed Malaysia’s readiness to host the IMT-GT meeting in September 2027 in Langkawi.
Meanwhile, in a joint statement, the ministers reaffirmed their commitment to the IMT-GT Vision 2036, which aims to create an integrated, innovative, inclusive, and sustainable subregion.
They noted that amid geopolitical uncertainties and growing trade fragmentation, there is a pressing need to strengthen resilience and capacity to respond to external disruptions.
The ministers also recognised artificial intelligence (AI) and digital transformation as strategic enablers of productivity, innovation, and competitiveness.
“In this regard, we remain committed to deepening cooperation across the three Focus Areas of Agriculture and Agro-based Industry, Tourism, and Halal Products and Services, supported by the five Enabler Focus Areas, to strengthen resilience and promote shared prosperity,” they said.
The joint statement further highlighted achievements under the IMT-GT Implementation Blueprint (IB) 2022-2026, particularly in gross domestic product (GDP) per capita, foreign direct investment (FDI), and international visitor arrivals, which surpassed the 2026 targets.
The GDP per capita increased from 21,646 current PPP$ in 2024 to 23,290 in 2025, while total trade in goods rose from US$708 billion (RM2.88 trillion) to US$810.8 billion (RM3.30 trillion).
FDI inflows increased from US$27.52 billion (RM112.1 billion) to US$28.44 billion (RM115.9 billion), while the unemployment rate declined from 3.8 per cent to 3.7 per cent, reflecting the subregion’s economic resilience.
“To address remaining gaps, we emphasise that the IB 2027-2031 should be anchored on three strategic goals - Economic Resilience, Integrated Networks, and Shared Prosperity - supported by stronger institutional coordination, stakeholder engagement, and robust monitoring and evaluation towards the achievement of Vision 2036,” it said. — Bernama

Title: Jalan Syed Putra-Jalan Istana intersection to close in stages from Sept 14
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 12 — A section of Jalan Syed Putra and Jalan Istana intersection here will be closed in stages starting September 14, from 10pm to 5am, to facilitate preliminary construction work for the New Pantai Expressway Extension Project (NPE 2).
New Pantai Expressway Sdn Bhd (NPE) announced in a statement today that the partial road closures and the implementation of temporary traffic management measures would be carried out in accordance with the construction schedule.
“Motorists are advised to plan their journeys in advance and to comply with all signage, instructions from traffic personnel, and the established traffic management measures,” the statement read.
NPE also reminded road users to adhere to safety guidelines and exercise increased caution when passing through the construction area.
“Motorists are also urged to follow the signage provided at the work site and to drive with extra care when passing through or approaching the construction zone,” the statement added.
Members of the public with inquiries or requiring further information regarding the construction work and traffic management may contact the NPE Infoline at 1300-88-1010. — Bernama

Title: Police arrest Sabah man on suspicion of murdering mother in Tambunan
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Sept 12 — Police arrested a 31-year-old man on suspicion of murdering his mother at a rented house in Kampung Katagayan, Tambunan, yesterday.
Keningau district police chief Supt Erwansyah Abdul Basir said police were alerted to the incident involving the 56-year-old victim at about 2pm and subsequently tracked down the suspect.
He said preliminary investigations found that the victim died at the scene from injuries believed to have been inflicted with a sharp weapon.
“Villagers apprehended the suspect at a hut in Kampung Sutung, Tambunan, before handing him over to police.
“The suspect was taken to the Tambunan police station, where he was arrested by the Criminal Investigation Department team from the Keningau district police headquarters,” he said in a statement today.
Erwansyah said the investigation team and forensic personnel had inspected the scene and seized several items believed to be linked to the case.
He said the victim’s body had been sent to the hospital for a post-mortem examination and the case was being investigated under Section 302 of the Penal Code.
“The public is urged not to speculate or spread unverified information about the case,” he said. — Bernama

Title: One-kilometre stretch of NSE lane closed near Ipoh as landslide precaution
Article:
IPOH, Sept 12 — The left lane of the North-South Expressway near a landslide at Kilometre 263.6 southbound will be closed along a one-kilometre stretch as a safety precaution, police said today.
Perak police chief Datuk Mohd Alwi Zainal Abidin said the closure would extend from Kilometre 262.8 to Kilometre 263.8, with safety cones placed along the route.
He said no contraflow lane had been activated and traffic conditions were being continuously monitored.
“CCTV cameras at the nearby vista point will be focused on the incident site to allow continuous monitoring of the landslide area and traffic flow along the route,” he said in a statement.
Police, PLUS Malaysia Berhad and other relevant agencies are continuing to monitor the site to ensure the safety of highway users.
Mohd Alwi advised motorists to follow instructions and safety signs, reduce their speed and drive carefully when passing through the area.
The Malaysian Highway Authority said yesterday that the slope collapse between the Menora Tunnel and Ipoh had caused congestion stretching up to 15 kilometres. — Bernama

Title: PM Anwar, Putin agree to establish mechanism to fast-track Malaysia-Russia deals
Article:
NEW DELHI, Sept 12 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, in a bilateral meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin, has suggested the establishment of a special mechanism between Putrajaya and Moscow to expedite the execution of all agreements reached between the two nations.
According to a note provided to Malaysian media, Putin agreed to the suggestion.
Both leaders also discussed about the import of Malaysian palm oil by Moscow and expediting direct flights between both countries during their meeting, held on the sidelines of the 18th Brics Leaders’ Summit here on yesterday.
During the 20-minute discussion, Anwar, who is also the Finance Minister, reiterated his appreciation for Russia’s support for energy cooperation with Malaysia.
It is to be noted that Petronas had engaged with Russian counterpart (Rosneft) and companies to advance collaboration in the sector.
Meanwhile, Russian news agency TASS quoted Putin as describing the 12.9 per cent growth in trade turnover between Russia and Malaysia last year as “a solid pace.”
“Last year, trade turnover between our countries grew by 12.9 per cent. That is a good pace,” he was quoted as saying.
The President emphasised that Moscow attaches great importance to contacts with Kuala Lumpur in the fields of education, science, technology, and tourism.
“During today’s conversation, we have the opportunity to discuss priority issues regarding our cooperation in all these areas,” the Russian leader noted, according to TASS.
Anwar arrived here yesterday to attend the 18th Brics Leaders’ Summit hosted by Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi.
Malaysia’s participation in the Brics Leaders’ Summit is in its capacity as a Brics partner country since January 1, 2025.
The meeting with Putin was Prime Minister’s first bilateral meeting here.
In 2024, total Asean-Russia trade amounted to US$18.1 billion, while Russian foreign direct investment in Asean totalled RM367.90 million (US$92.97 million).
For Malaysia, Russia was the country's ninth-largest trading partner among European nations in 2025, with total trade valued at RM8.72 billion (US$2.04 billion).
Malaysia’s primary exports to Russia included electrical and electronic products, machinery, equipment and parts, and processed food, while principal imports consisted of petroleum products, minerals, chemicals and chemical-based products. — Bernama

Title: ‘Slayyy’: PM Anwar turns ‘Guru’ for Malaysia’s Brics diplomatic mission
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 12 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim hopes Malaysia’s diplomatic mission at the 18th Brics Leaders’ Summit in India will achieve its objectives, while his light-hearted reference to himself as “Guru” in a Facebook post after arriving in New Delhi caught the attention of netizens.
Anwar said he was bringing Malaysia’s voice to the prestigious global platform, guided by the Madani Diplomacy framework.
“Alhamdulillah, Guru has safely arrived in New Delhi, India to represent the country on the world stage at the 18th Brics Leaders’ Summit.
“Please pray that this diplomatic mission achieves its objectives. May the students learn from Guru how Madani Diplomacy is put into practice. Slayyy,” he said in the post.
The aircraft carrying Anwar and his delegation landed at the Air Force Station (AFS) Palam, New Delhi at 6.30pm local time (9pm Malaysian time).
Tomorrow (September 13), the Prime Minister is scheduled to attend the opening session of the 18th Brics Leaders’ Summit and deliver a National Statement on Shaping the Future for Inclusive Global Growth.
The summit, hosted by Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi, carries the theme “Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability”, with a focus on strengthening resilience, economic cooperation as well as trade and investment reforms. — Bernama

Title: King renews Putin’s invitation to visit Malaysia through PM Anwar at Brics summit
Article:
NEW DELHI, Sept 12 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim conveyed warm regards from His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia to Russian President Vladimir Putin during their bilateral meeting here yesterday.
“Sultan Ibrahim sends his personal regards,” Anwar said.
The Prime Minister also reiterated Sultan Ibrahim’s invitation to Putin to make a state visit to Malaysia.
“Insya-Allah, this visit will open a new chapter in the increasingly close, mature, and mutually beneficial relationship between Malaysia and Russia,” Anwar said.
Sultan Ibrahim, who ascended the federal throne on January 31, 2024, has visited Russia three times.
His Majesty made a state visit to Russia in August 2025, followed by a special visit in January 2026 and a visit to Moscow in May for Russia’s Victory Day celebrations. — Bernama

Title: New school curriculum to introduce Sabah identity elements in Year One and Form One next year
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Sept 12 — Elements reflecting Sabah’s identity will be incorporated into the new school curriculum for Year One and Form One students from the next academic session, Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek said.
She said the initiative was among the agreements reached on education at the Malaysia Agreement 1963 Implementation Action Council (MTPMA63) meeting here this morning.
Fadhlina said Sabah Education, Science, Technology and Innovation Minister Datuk James Ratib had given his full support to the proposal.
“Among the matters discussed was how we can continue to support education in Sabah based on the agreements and terms under MA63.
“The Sabah identity elements will be introduced in the new Year One and Form One curriculum from next year,” she told reporters after attending the handover ceremony for the Sekolah Menengah Sains Sabah and Sekolah Kebangsaan Buit Hill projects here yesterday.
Fadhlina said incorporating elements of Sabah’s identity into the curriculum was important in strengthening ties among Sabah, Sarawak and Peninsular Malaysia, which she described as a foundation of Malaysia’s strength.
She said the initiative would enable younger generations to understand, appreciate and respect Sabah’s rich cultural heritage while allowing it to be shared more widely through the national curriculum.
Meanwhile, Fadhlina said the placement of new teachers and appointments of principals and headteachers in Sabah were in the final stages of being completed.
On dilapidated schools in Sabah, the minister said progress was encouraging, with some projects completed and others under construction or in the pre-implementation stage.
She said the ministry was continuing to closely monitor the projects with relevant agencies, including the Sabah Public Works Department (JKR), to ensure upgrading works proceeded smoothly.
In her speech earlier, Fadhlina said 245 dilapidated schools in Sabah had been fully rebuilt, while another 63 were under construction and the remainder were at various stages of implementation.
They are among 416 dilapidated schools in Sabah identified for complete replacement, she said. — Bernama

Title: Malaysia-Russia ties in focus as PM Anwar, Putin meet at Brics summit
Article:
NEW DELHI, Sept 12 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim and Russian President Vladimir Putin met on the sidelines of the 18th BRICS Leaders’ Summit here, providing an opportunity for both leaders to strengthen Putrajaya and Moscow’s relations and exchange views on matters of mutual interest.
It marked Anwar’s first bilateral meeting upon his arrival here to participate in the summit in Malaysia’s capacity as a BRICS partner country since January 1, 2025.
The meeting underscored the importance of maintaining high-level engagement between the two countries, particularly as Malaysia seeks to deepen economic and strategic ties with major emerging economies.
Malaysia and Russia have maintained longstanding diplomatic relations since 1967, with cooperation spanning trade and investment, energy, education, tourism, defence and other areas.
Both countries have also expressed interest in expanding bilateral economic engagement and exploring new areas of collaboration.
The meeting also came as Malaysia continues to advocate for a more inclusive and balanced international order while strengthening its engagement with the Global South through platforms such as BRICS and other multilateral mechanisms.
Anwar’s bilateral meeting with Putin further reinforced the commitment of both countries to constructive dialogue, closer cooperation and stronger people-to-people ties, while contributing to Malaysia’s broader foreign policy and economic objectives.
In 2024, total Asean-Russia trade amounted to US$18.1 billion, while Russian foreign direct investment in Asean totalled RM367.90 million (US$92.97 million).
For Malaysia, Russia was the country’s ninth-largest trading partner among European nations in 2025, with total trade was valued at RM8.72 billion (US$2.04 billion).
Malaysia’s primary exports to Russia included electrical and electronic products, machinery, equipment and parts, and processed food, while principal imports consisted of petroleum products, minerals, chemicals and chemical-based products. — Bernama

Title: Anwar welcomes Western push to ban trade with illegal Israeli settlements
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 12 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has welcomed the joint statement issued on September 8 by the foreign ministers of 12 Western countries regarding measures against illegal Israeli settlements.
He said the steps represent an overdue shift in the approach of several Western governments and must now be matched by firm implementation.
“These governments should use their considerable diplomatic and economic leverage over Israel to press for an end to settlement expansion and forced displacement, accountability for the devastation inflicted on Gaza and unimpeded humanitarian access,” he said in a Facebook post yesterday.
Anwar said he noted in particular that Britain, Canada and France would bring forward measures to ban trade in settlement goods, joining several European countries that have already taken this step.
“I also recognise the significance of the statement by British Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband to the House of Commons. The United Kingdom has now formally recognised the unlawfulness of the Israeli occupation as a whole.
“It has also acknowledged that ethnic cleansing of Palestinians is taking place in areas of the West Bank at the hands of what Mr Miliband rightly calls ‘settler terrorists’. These are significant acknowledgements, grounded in international law and in the realities confronting the Palestinian people,” he said.
Anwar called on the international community to move beyond statements towards concrete and binding measures that uphold international law, protect the rights of the Palestinian people and secure a just and lasting peace in the Middle East.
Canada, Denmark, Finland, France, Iceland, Ireland, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Spain, Sweden and the UK confirm their intention to introduce national and or support European restrictions on trade in goods with settlements which are illegal under international law, or that they are actively considering these and other measures, in accordance with their national procedures. — Bernama

Title: MCMC probes claims Claude AI targeted Malaysian voters, but says issue outside its mandate
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Sept 11 — The Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) is examining claims that Anthropic’s Claude artificial intelligence platform was used to operate a commercial election manipulation campaign targeting users in Malaysia.
MCMC said it took the US AI company’s latest report seriously but stressed that the activities described fell outside its functions and mandate.
“MCMC was not involved in any activities or dealings as described in the report,” it said in a statement today.
Anthropic reportedly said it had identified and removed an account linked to a network of about 1,000 fake accounts on X, a fake news website and several fabricated dossiers or intelligence files.
MCMC said it was seeking further information and clarification from the relevant parties to establish the facts and understand the context of the claims.
“Based on the information and evidence obtained, MCMC will determine the appropriate follow-up action within its jurisdiction, including working with the relevant authorities,” it said.
The commission added that protecting the public from online harm and maintaining a safe and trusted online environment remained central to its responsibilities. — Bernama

Title: Anwar to meet Modi, leading Indian companies on Brics summit sidelines today
Article:
NEW DELHI, Sept 12 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim is scheduled to have three bilateral meetings today on the sidelines of the 18th Brics Leaders’ Summit here.
The day starts off with a bilateral meeting with Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian, followed by one with Anwar’s Indian counterpart and summit host Narendra Modi.
His third bilateral meeting is with Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed.
The Prime Minister is also scheduled to have a pull aside meeting with Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev.
This will be followed by one-on-one business meetings, including with Adani Group, which has positioned itself to be the market leader in its transport logistics and energy utility portfolio businesses focusing on large scale infrastructure development in India.
Also lined up are Segula Technologies India Pvt Ltd, a global engineering group; AWL Agri Business Ltd, one of India’s largest food and fast-moving consumer goods companies; and Motherson Group, a leading global design, engineering, manufacturing, assembly, and logistics specialist.
Later in the day, the Prime Minister will attend a gala dinner for leaders of BRICS member, partner and outreach countries at the Bharat Mandapan, the exhibition and convention centre where the summit will take place.
The summit, themed “Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability”, will focus on strengthening resilience, economic cooperation as well as trade and investment reforms.
As a founding member of BRICS, India has previously held its chairship three times — in 2012, 2016 and 2021. India assumed its fourth BRICS chairship on January 1, 2026.
Malaysia’s participation in the BRICS Leaders’ Summit is in its capacity as a BRICS partner country since January 1, 2025. — Bernama

Title: KL DOE warns of fake procurement scams after two suppliers lose more than RM200,000
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 11 — The Kuala Lumpur Department of Environment (DOE) has detected several attempts by irresponsible parties to commit fraud using the department’s name.
Its Director, Sharifah Zakiah Syed Sahab, said that as of today, eight such cases have been detected involving government procurement order scams, resulting in losses totalling more than RM200,000 for two suppliers.
She said her department first detected the scam on September 4, when a representative of a diving equipment supplier came to the department to verify the authenticity of government procurement documents.
“Prior to that, KL DOE also received several inquiries regarding these government procurement documents starting in mid-August, and last Tuesday (September 8) from a supplier company representative who also came to inquire about a souvenir order worth more than RM100,000 supposedly made by KL DOE for an upcoming programme,” she told Bernama, here today.
She noted that checks by her department revealed that the department had never made any souvenir orders or programme bookings. Instead, the orders were made using forged documents that abused officers’ names, alongside fake letterheads and management signatures.
“Based on the suppliers’ information, they claimed to have transferred more than RM100,000 to certain parties as an advance payment for the souvenirs, and KL DOE has asked the suppliers to make a police report regarding the scam,” she said.
Elaborating further, she added that KL DOE also lodged a police report last Wednesday denying the involvement of department officers in the incident, while reports were also made to the DOE Headquarters Finance Division.
However, she mentioned that yesterday and today, her department still received inquiries regarding the fake procurement orders.
“In fact, today there was a supplier who was scammed with losses exceeding RM100,000, and the department has subsequently referred these cases further to the Bukit Aman Commercial Crime Investigation Department,” she said.
Sharifah Zakiah also advised all suppliers and contractors to be cautious and verify the authenticity of any government procurement documents they received. — Bernama

Title: Fire Dept: Two men found dead in separate incidents in Penang drain and Perak river
Article:
BUTTERWORTH, Sept 11 — Two men were found dead in separate incidents in Penang and Perak today, one in a drain near a school here and the other in Sungai Perak.
The body of Ooi Chai Siang, 37, was found in a drain about 1.5 metres deep near Sekolah Menengah Kebangsaan (SMK) Tun Hussein Onn in Taman Kelisa Emas here today.
Penang Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) Operations assistant director John Sagun Francis said the department received a call from the police at 12.10pm requesting assistance to retrieve the body.
“A team from the Perai Fire and Rescue Station (BBP) proceeded to the location and, upon arrival, found a man in the drain. The operation commander then instructed firefighters wearing full personal protective equipment (PPE) to retrieve the body,” he said in a statement today.
He said the body was handed over to the police for further action and later sent to the hospital for a post-mortem to determine the actual cause of death.
In Ipoh, the body of a 38-year-old man feared drowned after jumping into Sungai Perak to retrieve his boat, which had drifted away from a fish cage yesterday, was found this afternoon.
Perak JBPM Operations assistant director Sabarodzi Nor Ahmad said the body was found at 2pm, about four kilometres from the spot where he had jumped at Batu 18, Kampung Kuchai, near Bota Kiri.
“The search operation resumed this morning, involving 30 personnel, including the K9 Unit and Water Rescue Team (PPDA), within a six-kilometre radius along the river.
“The victim’s body was subsequently found floating by the PPDA team and brought ashore before being handed over to the police for further action,” he said in a statement today.
Earlier, Sabarodzi said the incident occurred at about 5pm yesterday when the man jumped into Sungai Perak to retrieve his boat. His nephew had attempted to rescue him, but the effort was unsuccessful. — Bernama

Title: PM Anwar heads to India for BRICS summit, bilateral talks with world leaders
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 11 — After concluding his working visit to Sabah today, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim departed for New Delhi to attend the 18th BRICS Leaders’ Summit, where he is also scheduled to hold several bilateral meetings.
In a Facebook post, Anwar said he was scheduled to meet the Prime Minister of India, as well as the presidents of Russia, Iran and Kazakhstan and the Prime Minister of Ethiopia.
“My delegation and I have departed for New Delhi, India to attend the 18th BRICS Leaders’ Summit.
“My itinerary in India also includes a visit to Keralam to meet the Grand Mufti of India to exchange views on community development, education and religious affairs,” he said.
After completing his diplomatic mission in India, Anwar will proceed to Malé, Maldives for an official visit at the invitation of President Dr Mohamed Muizzu.
“May everything go smoothly and may this visit bring tangible benefits to the people and the country. Insya-Allah,” he said. — Bernama
